'''Milton Kerker''' (September 25, 1920 — May 2, 2016) was an American [[Physical chemistry|physical chemist]] and former professor at department of chemistry at [[Clarkson University]]. He is best known for his work on [[aerosol]], [[interface and colloid science]], as well as for pioneering [[surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy]]. [[Kerker effect]] in optics is named after him.

==Biography==
Kerker was born on September 25, 1920, in [[Utica, New York]]. He received his A.B. in chemistry from [[Columbia University]] in 1941.<ref name="cen-acs"/> From 1942 to 1945, he was a member of [[United States Army]] and received [[Bronze Star Medal]] for his service.<ref name="kerker-obituary"/> He married his wife, Reva Stemerman, in 1946.<ref name="appreciation"/> Graduating from Columbia University with a PhD in chemistry in 1949, he joined [[Clarkson University]] as a professor in the same year. He acted as the chair of the department of chemistry from 1960 to 1964, as well as the dean of science from 1964 to 1966 and from 1981 to 1985. He retired from Clarkson University in 1991. Serving as the editor of ''[[Journal of Colloid and Interface Science]]'' from 1965 to 1992, he was also granted fellowships by [[Optica (society)|Optical Society]], [[American Chemical Society]] and [[Ford Foundation]].<ref name="kerker-obituary"/><ref name="appreciation"/> Kerker died on May 2, 2016, in [[Thousand Oaks, California]], U.S., and was survived by his wife and four children.<ref name="cen-acs"/> He was a contributor to ''[[Midstream (magazine)|Midstream]]'' magazine<ref name="kerker-obituary"/> and [[Jewish Theological Seminary of America]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=John |title=Dickens' greatest villain: The faces of Fagin |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/dickens-greatest-villain-the-faces-of-fagin-317786.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220515/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/dickens-greatest-villain-the-faces-of-fagin-317786.html |archive-date=2022-05-15 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=[[The Independent]] |access-date=November 15, 2021 |date=July 7, 2013}}</ref> as well as ''[[Isis (journal)|Isis]]'' journal.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kerker |first1=Milton |title=The Svedberg and Molecular Reality |journal=[[Isis (journal)|Isis]] |date=1967 |volume=67 |issue=2 |pages=190–216|doi=10.1086/351584 |s2cid=143732843 }}</ref>

Kerker's work encompassed [[aerosol]] and [[colloid]] science, as well as their relation to [[light scattering]] by small particles.<ref name="appreciation"/> He is known for authoring the 1969 textbook on the subject, ''The Scattering of Light and Other Electromagnetic Radiation''.<ref name="cen-acs"/><ref name="kerker-obituary"/> Regarded as a pioneer of [[surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy]] (SERS),<ref name="appreciation"/><ref name="cen-acs"/> he has worked on the mathematical models in the field.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kerker |first1=M. |last2=Wang |first2=D.-S. |last3=Chew |first3=H. |title=Surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) by molecules adsorbed at spherical particles |journal=[[Applied Optics]] |date=1980 |volume=19 |issue=19 |pages=3373–3388 |doi=10.1364/AO.19.003373|pmid=20234623 |bibcode=1980ApOpt..19.3373K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=D.-S. |last2=Kerker |first2=M. |title=Enhanced Raman scattering by molecules adsorbed at the surface of colloidal spheroids |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |date=1981 |volume=24 |issue=4 |page=1777 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.24.1777|bibcode=1981PhRvB..24.1777W }}</ref> In 1986, Kerker also coauthored the article on light scattering by hypothetical [[Magnetism|magnetic]] spheres, which hypothesized a distinct absence of [[backscatter]]ing for small particles with equal [[Relative permittivity|relative permittivities]] and [[Permeability (electromagnetism)|permeabilities]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kerker |first1=M. |last2=Wang |first2=D.-S. |last3=Giles |first3=C. L. |title=Electromagnetic scattering by magnetic spheres |journal=[[Journal of the Optical Society of America]] |date=1983 |volume=73 |issue=6 |pages=765–767 |doi=10.1364/JOSA.73.000765|bibcode=1983JOSA...73..765K }}</ref> While being largely unnoticed at the time of its publication, the work has since attracted attention with the advent of [[metamaterial]]s and [[nanophotonics]]; the associated phenomenon, named as [[Kerker effect]], was later verified experimentally.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Genevet |first1=Patrice |last2=Capasso |first2=Federico |last3=Aieta |first3=Francesco |last4=Khorasaninejad |first4=Mohammadreza |last5=Devlin |first5=Robert |author-link2=Federico Capasso |title=Recent advances in planar optics: from plasmonic to dielectric metasurfaces |date=2017 |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=139–152 |doi=10.1364/OPTICA.4.000139 |journal=[[Optica (journal)|Optica]]|doi-access=free |bibcode=2017Optic...4..139G }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Wei |last2=Kivshar |first2=Yuri S. |title=Generalized Kerker effects in nanophotonics and meta-optics |journal=[[Optics Express]] |date=2018 |volume=26 |issue=10 |pages=13085–13105 |doi=10.1364/OE.26.013085|pmid=29801341 |doi-access=free |hdl=1885/197175 |hdl-access=free |arxiv=1801.00092 }}</ref>
